summary: Reserved-pool throughput collapse following sudden tenant affinity spike causing GPU attach failures
description:
Issue summary:
During a busy midday window on 2026-03-12, LumaDocs observed a sudden and sustained drop in throughput on their dedicated reserved pool in us-east. Many requests returned transient 503 / attach-timeout errors and P99 latency spiked. The customer reported that the problem started after they rolled a heavier concurrent job in their app that coincided with a model pin migration.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency increased from p50~40ms to p50~250ms and p99 jumped to 6s+ for generation routes.
- ~25% of requests experienced attach failures or 5xx for a ~45 minute window.
- Affected customer: LumaDocs (dedicated reserved pool).

Environment:
- Deployment: dedicated reserved pool (customer LumaDocs)
- Region: us-east
- Models: redwood/gpt-3.5-medium, meta/llama-2-13b pinned for specific routes

Timeline / Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) 12:09 UTC: customer rolled an internal job that significantly increased short-lived stream concurrency and changed model pinning for a subset of traffic.
2) 12:12 UTC: internal autoscaler began increasing capacity but allocator attach latency started rising.
3) 12:15 - 12:35 UTC: intermittent 503/attach-timeouts and elevated p99, throughput dropped by ~40%.
4) 12:55 UTC: mitigation actions (auto-evict noisy sidecar, throttle customer ephemerals) applied; attach latency recovered and throughput normalized by 13:00 UTC.

Observed behavior / Logs / Metrics:
- Serving-runtime logs: repeated "attach timeout after 2500ms" and "prefetch lease wait > 5000ms" messages on several hosts.
- Allocator metrics: attach_latency_p95 increased to 4.8s on host-group A; attach_fail_rate spiked to 18%.
- Node metrics: connection_fds count for a handful of nodes rose 4x; small-stream fanout ratio increased sharply.
- KV-cache entries for LumaDocs grew 3x (their job created many unique prefixes), increasing memory pressure and prefetch churn.

Initial hypothesis:
- Sudden tenant affinity spike combined with a burst of many short-lived streams overloaded sidecars on several nodes. The sidecars opened many ephemeral connections which blocked allocator progress and serialized attach operations, leading to attach backoffs and throughput collapse.
- KV-cache growth increased prefetch pressure and memory churn, amplifying latency.

Actions taken so far:
- Support throttled the customer ephemeral burst via a temporary rate-limit override and recommended the customer reduce short-lived stream concurrency.
- SRE evicted the noisy sidecar processes on two affected hosts and forced reallocation to healthier nodes.
- Autoscaler was observed to spin up capacity but key hosts showed attach serialization; we applied a temporary scheduler-affinity relaxation to rebalance.

Workaround applied to customer:
- Applied conservative request concurrency cap for LumaDocs routes and disabled their aggressive prewarm hook for 30 minutes. Customer confirms traffic returned to baseline.

Next steps / Follow-ups captured below.
comments: 2026-03-12 12:22 UTC - Support (Aisha Patel): Initial triage - collecting logs and asking for customer QPS profile. Customer supplied trace IDs and recent deployment timeline.

2026-03-12 12:45 UTC - SRE (Liam Chen): Observed attach latency spike pinned to host-group A. Noted 4 nodes with fd explosion and high sidecar CPU. Evicted sidecars and started rebalancing; requested temporary throttle on customer concurrency.

2026-03-12 12:50 UTC - Customer (LumaDocs - Jenna Ortiz): Confirmed we rolled an internal batch of short-lived jobs and saw a flood of 200ms+ connection bursts. We've applied a client-side throttle as requested and will follow SRE guidance.

2026-03-12 12:58 UTC - SRE (Liam Chen): Throughput recovered to ~95% baseline after eviction and throttle. Still seeing elevated prefetch churn - likely KV-cache growth from new prefixes. Scheduling deeper allocator-level investigation.

2026-03-13 09:10 UTC - Eng (Priya Rao): Postmortem draft: root cause points to combined effects: (1) tenant affinity spike that clustered new short streams on few nodes, (2) sidecar connection handling creating attach serialization, (3) kv-cache expansion increasing prefetch work and memory contention.
2026-03-13 14:00 UTC - Support (Aisha Patel): Customer confirms no recurrence for 24h. Marking incident resolved; follow-ups listed below.
resolution: Mitigated - temporary throttle and sidecar eviction allowed allocator to rebalance; customer reduced short-lived stream concurrency and disabled an aggressive prewarm hook. Persistent fixes planned (see follow-up actions).
root_cause: A tenant-driven affinity spike created high short-stream fanout concentrated on a small set of hosts. Sidecars on those hosts opened excessive ephemeral connections, which serialized allocator attach work and increased prefetch/KV-cache churn, causing attach timeouts and throughput collapse.
workaround: Applied temporary concurrency caps for customer routes and evicted noisy sidecars on affected hosts. Autoscaler capacity added but scheduler affinity relaxation sped recovery.
follow_up_actions: Engineering: Add backpressure in sidecar connection handling to prevent fd explosion when many short streams start concurrently.
Platform: Improve allocator instrumentation to detect attach-serialization hotspots and trigger proactive host eviction or spread earlier.
Product: Recommend guidance in Dedicated onboarding docs about prewarm hooks and short-lived stream patterns for heavy concurrency customers.
SRE: Create a runbook for affinity-spike incidents with a checklist (identify fd-explosion hosts, evict sidecars, apply throttle, relax scheduler affinity).
Customer success: Review LumaDocs usage pattern and suggest pacing or pinning strategies to avoid future concentrated affinity spikes.
